chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Rahman, from his father, from Dawud ibn Farqad, who said:

I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'Eating carrots warms the kidneys and establishes the manhood.' I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! How can I eat it when I have no teeth?' So he said to me, 'Instruct the maid to boil it, and eat it.'
ai.seo_question: What are the health benefits of eating carrots according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) illustrates the Shia tradition of integrating practical health advice with spiritual authority, emphasizing the carrot's role in warming the kidneys and enhancing vitality. The specific instruction to boil the carrot for those without teeth reflects the broader Islamic medical principle of adapting dietary prescriptions to individual physical conditions, ensuring accessibility of medicinal benefits.
